sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: Alate head, pronotum and antennal segment 1 very dark brown, almost black, wings dark smoky, antennae 15-segmented, forewing membrane hairy and densely covered with mostly pointed microspines; the body is larger than in E. westraliensis and E. apiocephalus, which distinguishes it from both. Soldier dimorphic, major and minor; the posterior 2/3 of the head hemispherical in dorsal view, the nasus about 2/3 of the rest of the head; the major soldier is darker than the corresponding form of E. recalvus, with a narrower nasus and a less rounded head.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text:
(The original records hitherto undescribed, i.e. first description.) Head, pronotum and antennal segment 1 very dark brown, almost black; postclypeus, thorax, abdominal tergites and legs (except the tarsi and the apices of the tibiae) slightly paler; abdominal sternites paler than the tergites; wings dark smoky. Head medium-sized, vertex flat, hairs sparse and small. Compound eyes rather large and projecting. Ocelli small, projecting, far from the compound eyes. Fontanelle about as long as the ocelli, narrow posteriorly and wide anteriorly. Antennae 15-segmented; segment 2 about half of segment 1, distinctly narrower, nearly cylindrical; segments 3—5 variable: either segment 3 shortest and narrowest and segment 4 slightly shorter than segment 5, or segment 3 longer than segments 2 and 4 and segment 5 shortest. Postclypeus slightly more than half as long as wide. First tooth of the right mandible slightly longer and narrower than tooth 2; first tooth of the left mandible slightly longer than tooth 2, about equally wide. Pronotum with sparse small hairs, the anterior margin broad and shallowly concave, the anterior corners narrower, the sides oblique to the broadly rounded posterior margin, the posterior margin with a median notch. Posterior margins of meso- and metanotum broad and moderately deeply concave. Wings relatively large, most veins dark; radius present or absent, very short; forewing membrane hairy and densely covered with mostly pointed microspines.
Measurements: body length with wings 14.00—16.50 mm; body length without wings 6.50—7.75 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.50—1.66 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.84—0.92 mm; head width 1.36—1.40 mm; greatest diameter of compound eye 0.40 mm; ocellus length 0.12 mm; pronotum length 0.77 mm; pronotum width 1.24—1.36 mm; forewing length 12.50 mm; forewing width 3.00 mm.

sections.label: Soldier
sections.text:
Major: head mainly dark orange-red, the region behind the base of the nasus up to the line through the antennal sockets and the cheeks smoky brown, the apical half of the nasus dark rusty; thoracic and abdominal tergites dark brown, antennae and femora slightly paler; tibiae and tarsi white. Posterior 2/3 of the head hemispherical in dorsal view; nasus long, stouter at the base, about 2/3 of the rest of the head, evenly tapering to a sharp point. Apical half of the nasus, the rest of the head and the thorax and abdomen almost hairless. Head slightly concave in the middle in profile. Antennae 12—14-segmented, usually 13; segments 2 and 4 about equal in length, segment 2 narrower than segment 4, or segment 4 shortest of all; segment 3 longer than segments 2 and 4, about as long as segment 5. Almost every colony contains individuals with the segments beyond segment 6 longer. Mandibles usually without pointed teeth, sometimes with pointed teeth on one or both sides, in which case they are short and broad at the base. Minor (the original records hitherto undescribed): colour as in the major, differing in the proportionally narrower head (not hemispherical, narrowing more gradually to the nasus), the longer nasus (3/4 of the rest of the head), the usually more concave dorsal margin of the head in profile, and the 12—13-segmented antennae (segmentation as in the major); mandibles as in the major.
Measurements: major body length 4.90 mm, head length (to apex of nasus) 1.79 mm, head width 0.97 mm, pronotum width 0.55 mm; minor body length 3.96 mm, head length (to apex of nasus) 1.50—1.54 mm, head width 0.73 mm, pronotum width 0.44 mm.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text:
Head mainly dark orange-red as in the soldier, the frons as before but mottled with smoky brown patches, or the head and frons ochraceous brown; postclypeus paler than the frons; cheeks smoky brown below; thoracic and abdominal tergites ochraceous brown. Antennae 14 or 15-segmented; segment 3 usually the shortest of all. Postclypeus more than half as long as wide.
Measurements: body length 3.00—3.50 mm; head length (to apex of labrum) 1.32 mm; head length (to clypeofrontal suture) 0.73 mm; head width 1.02 mm; pronotum width 0.62 mm.

sections.label: Other
sections.text: The nest is built beneath low shrubs, up to 10 inches high and up to 12 inches in basal diameter; the galleries contain numerous small grey pellets (made of chewed grass) up to 0.75 mm in diameter, some composed entirely of grass fibres and others of fine gum particles and unrecognisable plant material. Alates were collected in nests at Darlot during the first week of December. Type locality Kalgoorlie.

note: Adapted from the species-level description in Hill (1942), originally in English; the original reads Eutermes tumuli, and the synonymy cites 1898 Eutermes tumuli Froggatt (partim), 1904 Termes (Eutermes) tumuli, 1912 Eutermes (Tumulitermes) tumuli Holmgren. The alate and the minor soldier are described by Hill for the first time. A footnote in the original points out that the caption of plate 35 does not agree with the figure, and that the species was redescribed (p. 410) as Mirotermes kalgoorliensis sp. nov. OCR misreadings: "tumult"="tumuli", "Terrnes"="Termes", "stemites"="sternites", "snail"="small", "ahdomen"="abdomen", "12-11+ segments"="12-14 segments", "fom"="form", "reoalvus"="recalvus", "apiooephalus"="apiocephalus", "ram"="mm", "Hamiterrruee"="Hamitermes", "Hololectotype"/"morpholectotype" are terms of the original.
